answer_1.quote: Conversational recommender systems (CRSs) aim to provide high-quality recommendation services through natural language conversations that span multiple rounds.
answer_1.outputs: responses in multi-turn conversations, recommendations, explanations

answer_2.quote: Following existing work, we adopt Recall@k to evaluate the recommendation subtask.

answer_3.quote: To reduce the need for humans, we propose an LLM-based scorer that can automatically give the score through prompting. Specifically, we use the text-davinci-003 model provided in the OpenAI API as the scorer with the conversation, explanation, and scoring rules concatenated as prompts.

answer_4.quote: We first invite five annotators to play the role of the system and engage in interactions with each user simulator. Then, we employ another two annotators to make pairwise evaluations, where one is generated by our simulator and the other comes from DialoGPT or the dataset.
answer_4.guideline: We count a win for a method when both annotators agree that its utterance is better; otherwise, we count a tie.
